core_obligations: Base cases: for l = 1 show that phi is injective exactly when the single scalar f generating phi(x_1) = f y_1 lies outside q and that Coker(phi) = R/(f, q), which gives the length identity by the definition of the order; then treat the diagonal case phi(x_i) = f_i y_i with f_i not in q by splitting into the l successive rank-one quotients, where length_R(Coker(phi)) = sum_i ord_{R/q}(f_i) and [phi(x_1),...,phi(x_l)] = f_1...f_l [y_1,...,y_l] by the admissible relation (b) (proof lines 17831-17858).

General induction setup: for l > 1 choose i minimal with phi(x_1) in <y_1,...,y_i> and argue by induction on i; for i = 1 conclude from the snake lemma applied to the displayed commutative diagram with exact rows and from induction on l (proof lines 17861-17880).

Rescaling and the length computation: for i > 1 write phi(x_1) = a_1 y_1 + ... + a_{i-1} y_{i-1} + a y_i with a not in q, define x'_j = x_j for j = 1 and a x_j for j >= 2 and y'_j = y_j for j < i and a y_j for j >= i, use the diagonal case to get length_R(M/M') = (l-1) ord(a) and length_R(N/N') = (l-i+1) ord(a), and chase the square M' -> M, N' -> N to obtain length_R(Coker(phi')) = length_R(Coker(phi)) + i ord(a) while f' = a^i f (proof lines 17881-17931).

Reduce to a = 1 and phi(x_1) = y_i: use the admissible relations for symbols to replace y_1,...,y_l by the sequence that is unchanged except that the i-th entry is replaced by a_1 y_1 + ... + a_{i-1} y_{i-1} + y_i, then use q x_1 = 0, hence q y_i = 0, and the third admissible relation to transpose y_i past y_{i-1}, which decreases i by one and closes the induction on i (proof lines 17931-17956).
proof_roadmap: Settle l = 1 and the diagonal case, where the cokernel splits into the successive quotients R/(f_i, q) and the determinant symbol multiplies the scalars (proof lines 17831-17858).
Run induction on l and on the minimal index i with phi(x_1) in <y_1,...,y_i>, handling i = 1 by the snake lemma (proof lines 17861-17880).

For i > 1 rescale the generating sequences by a, compare the lengths of M/M' and N/N' to get the change of length_R(Coker) and the change f' = a^i f, reduce to a = 1, then use the admissible relations to arrange phi(x_1) = y_i and transpose, decreasing i (proof lines 17881-17956).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the chapter's Key Lemma. Under the hypothesis that M and N each admit generating sequences x_1,...,x_l and y_1,...,y_l whose successive quotients are all isomorphic to R/q with dim(R/q) = 1, it asserts that phi : M -> N is injective if and only if phi_q is an isomorphism, and that then length_R(Coker(phi)) equals the order ord_{R/q}(f) of the residue-field element f defined by [phi(x_1),...,phi(x_l)] = f [y_1,...,y_l] in det_{kappa(q)}(N_q) (statement lines 17803-17828). The proof is a genuine double induction: the case l = 1 and the diagonal case phi(x_i) = f_i y_i with f_i not in q are disposed of first (proof lines 17831-17858); then for general l one lets i be minimal with phi(x_1) in <y_1,...,y_i>, rescales the x_j and y_j by a to reach a = 1 and computes length_R(M/M') = (l-1) ord(a) together with length_R(N/N') = (l-i+1) ord(a) to obtain length_R(Coker(phi')) = length_R(Coker(phi)) + i ord(a) while f' = a^i f, and finally uses the admissible relations of the determinant to replace y_1,...,y_l by the transposed sequence, which decreases the invariant i by one (proof lines 17861-17956). The coordination of the determinant condition with the length bookkeeping under a change of generating sequences is the crux of the argument and is not a routine exercise, so the claim is H3.
